newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish stocks outlook unclear as more floods loom.
newsitem.headline: Polish stocks outlook unclear as more floods loom.

text.p: The outlook for Polish shares was uncertain on Friday as many investors were expected to hold back, waiting to see whether the south of the country is hit by further flooding.

Analysts said that even though stronger buying after price fixing on Thursday might signal the market was recovering from flood concerns, uncertainty over the impact of flood aid efforts on the state budget and public finances might cap demand.@
The government has arranged a 2.5 billion zloty credit line from the central bank which has led to anxiety about its inflationary impact.

Some analysts saw some potential for a recovery in prices because losses from floods have been fairly limited, and because hopes that experience gained in the past two weeks should help limit damage from any second wave of flooding.
Polifarb Wroclaw, Rafako, ZEW and Viscoplast remained suspended due to flooding.
These companies operate mainly in southern Poland where much of the flooding has occurred.
They were suspended as the exchange decided that investors had insufficient access to information about the difficulties they were experiencing.
